title: Go and Terraform Shared-file Probe Implementation Plan
agentic_workers: After review, use superpowers:subagent-driven-development, preserving the previously requested parallel-agent approach. Execute dependent tasks in order; independent fixture and packaging work may run in parallel. Track each step with done=true. Do not commit.
goal: Determine whether a small Go CLI and a custom Terraform provider can preserve Cook's shared-file lifecycle while reusing Terraform composition, saved plans and state.
architecture: Keep composition in Terraform modules, place shared-block reconciliation in a small Go domain package, and expose it through one generic provider resource per file. Keep the Go CLI as a facade over terraform-exec. Compare the same fixtures against the existing Groovy implementation and report lifecycle and runtime costs before choosing a replacement.
global_constraints: Use main branch and do not commit.
Keep plan, specification and evidence as JSON and native source files under cookbook; create no Markdown files.
Keep the current Groovy core and ingredient builds available throughout the comparison.
Use only temporary target repositories and local providers; execute no cloud resources or agent sessions.
Go toolchain: 1.26.7. Terraform executable: 1.15.5. Existing local_file baseline provider: hashicorp/local 2.9.1.
Probe dependencies: terraform-exec v0.25.3 and terraform-plugin-framework v1.18.0; record transitive dependencies in go.sum.
Probe provider artifact: registry.terraform.io/the-cook/cook 0.1.0, installed from a local filesystem mirror.
Supported probe build targets: linux/amd64, linux/arm64, darwin/amd64, darwin/arm64; CGO_ENABLED=0.
Ingredient versions remain independent from engine and provider versions.
owns defaults to false; Git is an explicit consumer of exported paths.
Codex and Claude are not classified as ingredients by this probe.

steps.signature: Reconcile(current Snapshot, prior Ownership, desired []Block) (Proposal, error); Release(current Snapshot, prior Ownership) (Proposal, error)
steps.approach: Scan anchored markers and preserve untouched byte spans. Version ownership as 1. Reject duplicate/nested/malformed markers and invalid UTF-8. Record adoption originals once; do not normalize CRLF or manual text.

steps.signature: Read(root, relative string) (Snapshot, error); Apply(root, relative string, proposal Proposal) error
steps.approach: Reject absolute paths, '..', .git/.cook destinations and symlink ancestors. Use a cooperating lock under .cook/terraform-probe only during apply; recheck existence/hash/mode while locked, then use atomic replacement. Default new files to 0644; never write during Read or planning. A lock does not establish ownership across Terraform states.

steps.expected: PASS for every pure lifecycle fixture and each rejected-write inventory check.

steps.check: filemodel imports neither repository nor Terraform; repository consumes filemodel and owns all filesystem effects.

tasks.title: Expose one generic Terraform resource per shared file

produces: tfprovider.New(version string) provider.Provider
provider cook schema: root string, an existing absolute temporary repository path.
resource cook_managed_blocks schema: path string; owns optional bool default false (true rejected in this probe); blocks map of {lines:list(string), adopt:optional(bool=false)}; id computed string.
Resource implements Resource, ResourceWithConfigure and ResourceWithModifyPlan, with all framework lifecycle signatures unchanged.
Private state key cook_ownership contains version-1 Ownership; cook_proposal contains the preview Snapshot and proposed Ownership.
Local provider binary terraform-provider-cook_v0.1.0, protocol 6.

steps.signature: tfprovider.New(version string) provider.Provider; managed-block resource framework Configure/Schema/ModifyPlan/Create/Read/Update/Delete methods
steps.approach: Use Framework v1.18.0. Store adoption baselines in provider private state. Plan a proposal with the pure reconciler and apply that exact proposal. Read checks managed bytes and preserves the resource identity on drift. Refuse markers that indicate an existing unadopted file claim. Competing initial creates are serialized and fail their preview recheck. On destroy, keep resp.Plan null, obtain the path from req.State, and capture the preview in response.Private. Terraform 1.15.5 and Framework v1.18.0 source support this handoff, but Step 4 must prove it using a saved real plan.

Probe CLI: cook-tf-probe plan --terraform PATH --recipe DIR --repo DIR --bundle DIR --observe .gitignore --var manager=npm
Probe CLI: cook-tf-probe apply --terraform PATH --repo DIR --bundle DIR
Bundle files: plan.tfplan, plan.json (terraform show JSON), metadata.json; version 1.

CLI --recipe must point to a staged temporary root module. Integration stages ingredients beside the recipe to preserve local module paths; the probe does not execute directly in the original cookbook sources.

assertions: Plan leaves the target byte/mode inventory unchanged.
Edit a manual suffix after a saved removal plan; apply returns preview_drift and preserves all bytes.
Mutating the plan binary or its repository binding is rejected.
Every path in planned/prior cook resources must appear in ManagedPaths; omitted or unknown paths fail planning.
Symlink replacement and chmod after preview reject apply before Terraform writes.

steps.expected: FAIL: missing driver or saved-plan bundle implementation.

steps.action: Implement SDK planning and bundle validation
steps.signature: Plan(ctx context.Context, config Config) (Bundle, error); Apply(ctx context.Context, config Config) error
steps.approach: Use tfexec Init, Plan with Out, ShowPlanFile and Apply with DirOrPlan. WorkDir is a temporary staged Terraform recipe directory supplied by the test/CLI; record its canonical path in metadata for apply, and keep it outside the target repository. Snapshot explicitly observed paths before and after planning; require both snapshots to match, and validate coverage against prior/planned resource paths. Hash the binary plan and bind metadata to the canonical repository. Apply reads WorkDir from the saved bundle, verifies the complete observed inventory, then invokes Terraform; the provider performs its own locked per-file recheck.
Use Go flag parsing; pass typed variables through an exact JSON var file. Require the Terraform path and saved bundle explicitly. These temporary probe flags do not decide the production Cook UX.

steps.action: Run saved-plan and SDK integration tests
steps.expected: PASS all stale-plan rejections, complete observation coverage and real apply-from-saved-plan checks.

steps.action: Review the execution path without committing
steps.check: Apply does not call Plan. All subprocess calls use terraform-exec; no unsupported Terraform Core imports.
